evals.prompt: Design QA test cases for this feature. Ticket LIN-482: 'Users can apply a coupon code at checkout. A valid, unexpired, unused coupon reduces the cart subtotal.' The repo has this validation in app/models/coupon.rb: `validates :subtotal_threshold, numericality: { greater_than_or_equal_to: 10 }` and the checkout controller checks `cart.subtotal >= coupon.subtotal_threshold` before allowing redemption. No Figma link or screenshot was provided, and there's no Figma MCP connected in this session. A .eagerworks/design-qa-test-cases.json already exists with testCases.scope set to ["manual", "automated"].
evals.expected_output: The plan includes a happy-path case for AC-1, boundary cases at $9.99 (rejected) and $10.00 (accepted) derived from the actual validation, and marks any layout/visual case under a '⚪ Not verifiable without more input' section rather than describing a checkout page layout that was never shown.
expectations: Response includes boundary test cases at exactly $9.99 and $10.00, citing the validates numericality rule as the source rather than a round number like $0 or $100
Response does not describe or assume any specific visual layout, styling, or UI copy for the coupon field since no design source was provided
Response explicitly states that design/visual cases are not verifiable without a Figma link or screenshot rather than silently omitting them
Response does not fabricate a Figma frame or screenshot content that was never given

evals.prompt: Design QA test cases for the feature described at https://mycompany.atlassian.net/browse/PROJ-991. There is no Jira MCP connected in this session and the `jira` CLI is not installed, so that URL cannot actually be fetched.
evals.expected_output: The response does not invent acceptance criteria from the URL or ticket key alone. It explains the ticket can't be fetched (no Jira integration reachable) and asks the user to paste the ticket's text or description instead of guessing what PROJ-991 might contain.
expectations: Response does not invent or guess acceptance criteria for PROJ-991 based on the URL or ticket number alone
Response explicitly states it could not fetch the ticket (no Jira MCP or CLI reachable)
Response asks the user to paste the ticket's text/description rather than proceeding with assumptions
Response does not produce a full test-case plan before receiving the actual feature description

evals.prompt: Design test cases for this AC: 'Expired coupons are rejected.' There's no other detail in the ticket about what counts as expired, and the codebase has a `Coupon#expired?` method that just checks `expires_at < Time.current` with no timezone handling visible in the diff.
evals.expected_output: The response flags that 'expired' is ambiguous with respect to timezone (server UTC instant vs. the user's local calendar day) and raises it as an open question for the PO rather than silently picking one interpretation and writing a boundary case around it.
expectations: Response identifies that the AC does not specify whether expiry is evaluated in UTC or the user's local timezone
Response raises this as an explicit open question for the PO rather than silently assuming one interpretation
Response does not fabricate a precise boundary test case (e.g. 'test at exactly 23:59:59 user-local time') as if the ambiguity were resolved
Response still produces a general negative-path case that an expired coupon is rejected, separate from the unresolved boundary question

evals.prompt: Design QA test cases for this feature: 'Add a `updated_at` timestamp badge to the admin dashboard header showing when the page's data was last refreshed. It's read-only, has no user input, is fed from an already-existing, already-tested `Dashboard#last_refreshed_at` method, and only appears in the admin dashboard header.'
evals.expected_output: A small, honest plan: a couple of happy-path cases (badge shows a formatted timestamp, updates on refresh) and no invented boundary, permission, state-machine, or integration cases, since none of those apply to a read-only display fed by an already-tested method. The response does not pad the plan with unrelated generic QA checklist items to look thorough.
expectations: Response produces a small number of cases (roughly 2-4) rather than padding the plan to look more thorough
Response does not invent boundary, permission-matrix, or state-transition cases for a feature that has no bounded input, no roles, and no state machine
Response does not add generic checklist items (e.g. 'test on mobile', 'check loading spinner') that don't trace to anything this specific feature touches
Response's cases each trace to either the stated behavior or a code signal, not to a generic QA checklist

Response does not list this case as 'New' or as an uncovered gap requiring QA effort

evals.prompt: Design QA test cases for coupon voiding. The repo has this Rails policy: `class CouponPolicy < ApplicationPolicy; def void?; user.admin_of?(record.organization); end; end`. There is no other permission check on this action anywhere else in the code.
evals.expected_output: The plan includes a permissions case for an admin of the coupon's organization succeeding at voiding it, and a case for a non-admin member of the same organization being denied — the two roles the policy actually distinguishes — without inventing a full cross product of every conceivable role (e.g. a 'super-admin' or 'guest' role that doesn't appear anywhere in the code).
expectations: Response includes a case where an org admin can void the coupon (allowed)
Response includes a case where a non-admin member of the same organization is denied
Response cites the CouponPolicy#void? method as the source of the permission rule
Response does not invent additional roles (e.g. 'super-admin', 'guest', 'billing-only') that have no corresponding check in the given code

evals.prompt: Design QA test cases for coupon status changes. The repo has: `enum status: { draft: 0, active: 1, expired: 2, redeemed: 3 }` on the Coupon model, with the only code paths being: draft -> active (via an activate! method), active -> redeemed (via a redeem! method), and active -> expired (via a scheduled job). No code path exists for redeemed -> active or expired -> redeemed.
evals.expected_output: The plan includes cases for each legal transition (draft->active, active->redeemed, active->expired) as happy paths, plus negative cases asserting that redeemed->active and expired->redeemed are not possible (e.g. calling activate! on a redeemed coupon has no effect or raises), since those transitions exist in the enum's cross-product but have no supporting code path.
expectations: Response includes happy-path cases for draft to active, active to redeemed, and active to expired transitions
Response includes at least one negative case asserting that redeemed to active is not possible
Response includes at least one negative case asserting that expired to redeemed is not possible
Response does not claim transitions exist that were not described in the code (e.g. draft to redeemed directly)
